summary: The Chinese Government Scholarship is a set of awards from the Chinese government, run by the China Scholarship Council, for citizens of other countries who want to study or do research at universities in China. It covers degree study at bachelor's, master's and doctoral level and two non-degree categories, general scholar and senior scholar. Awards come through two kinds of route: Type A, which is organised through national authorities such as an embassy or consulate, and Type B, which is organised by Chinese universities. What the award pays is set per component (tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, medical insurance); each component is described separately below.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be citizens of a country other than China and be in good physical and mental health. They must also meet the entry requirements of the Chinese university they apply to, including academic ability and language level. Some embassy channels take applications only from their own citizens (for example the Montreal consulate notice is for Canadian citizens) and one embassy states that it gives priority to local applicants; check the notice of the channel you use.

Education level and age (the age limits are applied as limits at application): bachelor's - high school graduate, under 25; master's - bachelor's degree holder, under 35; doctoral - master's degree holder, under 40; general scholar - at least a high school graduate, under 45; senior scholar - master's degree holder or associate professor or above, under 50. Type B university routes that are for graduate study state master's under 35 and doctoral under 40.

Language: for Chinese-taught bachelor's and general scholar programmes HSK level 3 is needed (applicants to Chinese language study programmes are exempt); Chinese-taught senior scholar programmes need HSK level 3; Chinese-taught master's and doctoral programmes need HSK level 4. Programmes taught in another language need a language certificate such as IELTS or TOEFL at the level the university requires. One Indonesian-embassy notice also exempts applicants who hold a Chinese-taught degree from a Chinese university. Several Type B universities set a higher Chinese level (for example HSK 5 with at least 180 points) or their own English scores, so check the university guide.

Test for bachelor's applicants: from the 2026/27 round, applicants to Chinese bachelor's degree programmes must take the China Scholastic Competency Assessment (CSCA) before applying and upload a valid score report. For September 2026 entry the sessions were 21 December 2025 and 25 January 2026. One notice states the test date must be after 1 March 2025. Applicants should check with the target university which test subjects it requires.

Other conditions stated: applicants cannot hold another Chinese government scholarship or a scholarship from the admitting university at the same time (one-off awards are excluded); concealing funding status leads to disqualification and, in one notice, a three-year ban on applying for the Chinese Government Scholarship; applicants under 18 need valid documents from a legal guardian in China; applicants who are former Chinese nationals, or who come from mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan and later took foreign nationality, may be asked for extra proof (for example proof of giving up the earlier nationality) by the host university.

Embassy channels warn that the China Scholarship Council has not authorised any individual or agent to handle applications.
age_experience_notes: Age limits: bachelor's under 25; master's under 35; doctoral under 40; general scholar under 45; senior scholar under 50. Senior scholar applicants need a master's degree or an associate professor post or above. No minimum work experience is stated in the notices read.
funding_summary: The award is made up of separate components: tuition, a free university dormitory or an accommodation subsidy, a monthly stipend and comprehensive medical insurance. International travel is not covered. A university guide quotes stipend rates of CNY 2,500 a month at bachelor's level, CNY 3,000 for master's and general scholar, and CNY 3,500 for doctoral and senior scholar. A university describing Type B awards says a partial award can cover only some of the components. For Type A awards from a national channel, the notice states that the award covers only the academic year named in the call, so study after that year has to be funded by the host university. University guides describe funding for a one-year Chinese preparatory course plus the standard length of the programme where a Chinese-taught degree requires it.
programmes_note: The notices read do not give one fixed list of fields. Each Chinese university decides which majors it offers to scholarship holders, and the list differs by university and by Type A or Type B route. In the application system, applicants pick a discipline field and major from a catalogue; universities are matched automatically to the student category and preferred teaching language, and applicants should check each university's own site for the majors open to them. Some national quotas focus on certain fields (the Indonesian quota names marine, medical, health, tourism and education majors, among others). Silk Road programmes at some universities are limited to named majors; an example is a bachelor's in New Energy Science and Engineering and a master's in Power Engineering and Engineering Thermophysics at one Hunan university.
institutions_note: Many Chinese universities take part, and the list is kept in the CSC application system. For Type A, applicants name target universities in the CSC online application (some guides ask for the university to be listed as first choice), and the CSC may adjust the university, major or award category. Embassy notices say applicants should contact their chosen universities and get at least one pre-admission document (a pre-admission notice or an invitation letter from a school or professor). For Type B, applicants apply to one university directly; the university picks candidates and recommends them to the CSC; each applicant may be put forward by only one university per year in the guides read. Universities whose own guides were read for this entry: Beijing Language and Culture University, Sun Yat-sen University, Jilin University, Tsinghua University, Northeast Normal University, Beijing Foreign Studies University, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Shanghai International Studies University, University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, Northwest A&F University and Changsha University of Science and Technology. This is not a complete list.

summary.detail: For high school graduates under 25. Chinese-taught programmes need HSK level 3 (Chinese language study is exempt); all bachelor's applicants need a valid CSCA score report. Majors depend on the university. One Type A guide describes one year of Chinese preparatory study before a Chinese-taught major where needed.

summary.detail: For master's degree holders under 40. Chinese-taught programmes need HSK level 4; other programmes need IELTS, TOEFL or similar as the university requires. Two recommendation letters and a study plan of at least 800 words are required in the national notices. Universities state a standard length of about 4 to 5 years.

Two non-degree categories. General scholar: at least a high school graduate, under 45; Chinese-taught programmes need HSK level 3 unless the applicant studies Chinese language. Senior scholar: master's degree holder or associate professor or above, under 50; Chinese-taught programmes need HSK level 3. Study plan of at least 500 words. One university guide gives the length of such study as half a year or one year.

Stated in an embassy notice and in a Type B university guide: travel costs are borne by the student.

benefits.limit_text: Funding from a single application covers the academic year named in the call
benefits.conditions: A national-channel notice states study beyond that year must be funded by the host university. Universities describe an annual review; failing it can lead to suspension or end of the award.

requirements.text: Scholarship application form, completed in Chinese or English in the online application system. Applicants must print or download the form after submitting.

Clear scan of the passport information page. The passport must be valid at least 12 months from the expected study start date (renew first if not); a notice allows other identity documents in exceptional cases if the receiving agency approves.
Notarized copy of the highest diploma; prospective graduates give official proof of student status. Documents not in Chinese or English need a notarized translation.
Academic transcripts, with a notarized translation if not in Chinese or English.
Valid HSK report for Chinese-taught programmes; IELTS, TOEFL or similar for programmes in other languages, as each university requires.
CSCA score report with a valid score; the test must be taken before the application deadline. Required test subjects depend on the university.
Pre-admission document from the university: a pre-admission notice or an invitation letter from a school or professor. One embassy asks for at least one such document from a university applied to.

Study plan or research proposal in Chinese or English: at least 200 words for bachelor's, 500 words for non-degree, 800 words for postgraduate. Some universities ask for more (for example 1,000 words).
Two recommendation letters from professors or associate professors, in Chinese or English.
Portfolio of work, uploaded in the system or sent to the universities directly.
Valid documents of a legal guardian in China.
Foreigner Physical Examination Form completed in English, fully filled in, signed by the doctor, stamped by the hospital and with a sealed photo; valid for six months. Incomplete forms are invalid.

requirements.text: Non-criminal record certificate from the local public security authority, usually issued within six months before submission.

application_steps.title: Choose your route: Type A or Type B
application_steps.detail: Type A is run through national authorities such as an embassy or consulate (bilateral and similar programmes); Type B is run by a Chinese university, mostly for master's and doctoral applicants. Your channel sets the deadline, agency number and any interview. Check the notice of your own country's embassy or the university guide.

application_steps.title: Pick universities and get a pre-admission document
application_steps.detail: Look up majors in the application system and on the university sites, then contact the universities or professors to get a pre-admission notice or invitation letter before you apply. Embassy notices say you should do this yourself; no agent is authorised.

application_steps.title: Take the CSCA if you apply for a bachelor's degree
application_steps.detail: Register for the China Scholastic Competency Assessment and take it before the deadline; you upload the score report with your application. Check which subjects the university needs. For September 2026 entry the test days were 21 December 2025 and 25 January 2026.

application_steps.title: Apply online in the CSC application system
application_steps.detail: Register, complete and save your personal details, choose the program category (Type A or Type B) and enter the agency number of your embassy or university; the category and number must match or the application is not processed. Add the study plan and language proof, upload clear, valid documents and submit. After submission you can withdraw, edit and resubmit only before processing starts. Print the application form.

application_steps.title: Send what your channel asks for
application_steps.detail: Rules differ by channel. Some embassies take only the online application and ask for no paper copy; some ask you to email the document package or the application serial number; the Montreal route asks for a French-language motivation letter and electronic documents to a Quebec ministry. For Type B you also apply in the university's own system, which may charge a fee after the first review.

application_steps.title: Embassy or university screening and interview
application_steps.detail: The embassy or consulate checks documents and eligibility, and some hold an online interview (for example a Polish-embassy notice sets interview invitations, confirmation and an interview within a fixed window, and excludes late or incomplete files; a US notice schedules interviews before decisions). For Type B the university reviews, may test or interview, and nominates candidates.

application_steps.title: Review by the China Scholarship Council
application_steps.detail: The embassy or university sends its recommended list to the CSC. The CSC has designated universities and experts check eligibility and academic performance, then decides the final list and may adjust the university, major, award category or duration. Guides describe the assessment as covering academic performance, overall competence and development potential. Results go back through the embassy or the university.

application_steps.title: University admission decision
application_steps.detail: The host university also decides admission from the application and its own capacity, and may suggest a change of major. In one national round, results were published in the system around July and August of the entry year, when winners downloaded the admission notice and the JW201 visa form.

application_steps.title: Collect admission documents and apply for the visa
application_steps.detail: Download or receive the admission notice and the JW201 form, then apply for a Chinese student visa. Register on the date in the admission notice; late registration without approval can end the admission and the scholarship, and early registration is not allowed.

application_steps.title: Pass the arrival checks and annual review
application_steps.detail: Students go through a review and a physical examination on arrival; failing the physical can cancel the award. All holders take an annual review covering academic performance, learning attitude, attendance and conduct; a failed review can lead to suspension or end of the scholarship. Holders in principle cannot change university, major or study length.

application_steps.title: Keep to the funding rules
application_steps.detail: Do not hold another Chinese government scholarship or a university scholarship at the same time (one-off awards excepted). Holding one wrongly can mean cancellation and return of money received. Funding from one application covers the academic year in the call; later years must be funded by the host university where a national notice says so.
